neighbours.label: the relative word after a vague head noun: 'something in me that', 'things that', 'ways that', 'go where'; the complementizer that ('said that') stays quiet
fire: The teacher noticed something in her that nobody else had seen.
This rule lets us do things that would otherwise be impossible.
He ran the club in ways that its founders had never imagined.
The explorers dared to travel where nobody had been.
Artists see beauty where others see only junk.
She wants something which truly belongs to another person.
What do you see in him that made you hire him?
We shouldn't count on things that may never happen.
quiet: The teacher told her parents that nobody else had come.
This rule says that we must arrive by nine.
He ran the club and its founders thanked him.
The explorers hoped that nobody would follow them.
Artists sold paintings and others bought only frames.
She knows that this truly belongs to another person.
What did you think that he said to you?
We agreed that the meeting may never happen.

short: relative after a vague noun ('things that')
